SafeLink sits in front of links from chat and social apps. It blocks deletion and account-takeover links, and it warns you when a link looks unsafe.

When a link needs a cloud check, SafeLink sends the address to its own server. The server asks threat-intelligence services and does not keep query strings (the part after a question mark), which is where login tokens often hide. SafeLink does not ask for your phone number or account name. Scan history stays on this phone and you can delete it. Some links are checked only on the phone and are never sent.

Android will not let an app silently take every link. Open the settings below, allow SafeLink to open supported links, and choose SafeLink when a chat app asks which app should open a link. Links that stay inside an in-app browser are not visible to SafeLink. You can also paste a link on the home screen.
